fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Detached Structure; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation; Detached Structure Complexity
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the street in both directions.
• Trim vegetation along the front driveway to maintain clear sightlines and at least 14 feet of vertical clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move quickly between the two buildings.
• Post the address visibly on the detached structure if it sits far from the street or is not visible from the main driveway approach.
• Clear dense vegetation away from the walkway connecting the residence to the detached structure so responders can move through without obstruction.
• Keep the rear access point unlocked or mark it clearly so responders can locate and use it quickly without circling the property.
• Mark any rear gate or secondary access point with a reflective indicator visible at night.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear enough that emergency vehicles can stage or turn around without being blocked by parked cars.
• Cut back shrubs or plantings along the perimeter fencing that block responder movement around the sides of the residence.
• Confirm that a gate, gap, or opening in the perimeter fencing provides access to the rear yard from at least one side of the property.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Green Space; Scattered Shrubs; Multiple Access Routes; Limited Rear Access
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters closest to the structure to create open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove or trim shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near the structure to reduce the chance of fire climbing from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Keep the area beneath tree clusters clear of dead leaves, fallen branches, and dry plant material.
• Maintain open spacing between scattered trees and any shrub growth below them so fire cannot travel easily from low plants up into the trees.
• Clear dead or dry plant material from the base of scattered shrubs across the property.
• Keep rear access clear of overhanging branches and low vegetation to allow movement around the back of the structure.
• Trim any branches from scattered trees that hang over or near the roofline or gutters.
• Maintain the open green space areas by keeping grass mowed short, especially where it connects to tree clusters or shrub areas near the structure.
